passages.text: Therefore, if you wish to become a garment of the divine spirit, first make every effort to strip off the filthy hold already laid on you (which is an unclean spirit) and the defiled covering. You cannot strip this off in any other way unless you are first baptized on the basis of good deeds and in this way, having become clean in both body and soul, enjoy the eternal kingdom that is to come. Therefore, do not put your trust in idols or share a defiled table with them. Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not hate those whom it is not right to hate, do not steal, and do not set yourselves to any evil deeds at all. Otherwise, deprived of the hope of the good things to come, in the present you will be beset by both evil demons and painful afflictions, while in the eternal age to come you will be punished with fire. What has been said to you today is sufficient. Now, those of you troubled by afflictions, remain for healing; among the others, those who wish may go in peace.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἔνδυμα οὖν εἰ βούλεσθε γενέσθαι θείου πνεύματος
lexical_decisions.chosen: if you wish to become a garment of the divine spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the source’s image of people becoming the spirit’s garment rather than merely being clothed by the spirit.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the filthy hold already laid on you
lexical_decisions.rationale: In context πρόλημμα denotes a prior possession or seizure, identified immediately as an unclean spirit; “preconception” would obscure that contextual image.

lexical_decisions.chosen: you are baptized on the basis of good deeds
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes ἐπί with the dative as expressing a basis or condition. Other viable nuances are “in connection with good deeds” or “with a view to good deeds.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ οὕτω καθαροὶ σώματί τε καὶ ψυχῇ γενόμενοι
lexical_decisions.chosen: and in this way, having become clean in both body and soul
lexical_decisions.rationale: Renders οὕτω as “in this way,” preserving its manner or result connection with the preceding statement that the covering cannot be removed in any other way.

lexical_decisions.chosen: do not hate those whom it is not right to hate
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the source’s qualification rather than broadening it into an unqualified prohibition of all hatred.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπό τε κακῶν δαιμόνων καὶ χαλεπῶν παθημάτων συνελασθήσεσθε
lexical_decisions.chosen: you will be beset by both evil demons and painful afflictions
lexical_decisions.rationale: συνελαύνω depicts being driven together, hemmed in, or hard-pressed; “beset” conveys that force naturally.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν δὲ τῷ ἐσομένῳ αἰῶνι αἰδίῳ κολασθήσεσθε πυρί
lexical_decisions.chosen: while in the eternal age to come you will be punished with fire
lexical_decisions.rationale: Attaches αἰδίῳ to the immediately preceding αἰῶνι, with which it agrees, preserving the contiguous phrase “eternal age.” Because αἰδίῳ can also agree with πυρί, “with eternal fire” remains a viable alternative.

source_issues.issue: The force of ἐπί with the dative is contextually open: it may express basis or condition, association, or purpose. The main rendering selects basis, while “with a view to good deeds” remains viable. No alteration of the supplied text is required.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐν δὲ τῷ ἐσομένῳ αἰῶνι αἰδίῳ κολασθήσεσθε πυρί
source_issues.issue: The dative adjective αἰδίῳ can modify either αἰῶνι or πυρί because both nouns are dative singular forms compatible with it. The main text follows the immediate attachment to αἰῶνι: “in the eternal age to come you will be punished with fire.” Alternatively, αἰδίῳ may form an adjective–noun phrase with πυρί across the intervening verb: “in the coming age you will be punished with eternal fire.” This is an attachment ambiguity, not evidence of source corruption.
